ai.definition: Cognitive RPA (Robotic Process Automation) integrates generative AI, particularly large language models and computer vision, into traditional RPA systems. This integration enables the software bots to handle unstructured data and adapt to variable user interface changes more effectively.
ai.howItWorks: Cognitive RPA combines computer vision for visual recognition of UI elements with natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning algorithms from large language models (LLMs). These technologies allow the bot to interpret the context and semantics of screen elements, making it capable of handling tasks that require understanding unstructured data or adapting to dynamic interfaces.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional RPA struggles with tasks involving unstructured data and changing user interfaces. Cognitive RPA addresses these limitations by enabling bots to understand and interact with complex, variable environments more flexibly.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training the AI models used in cognitive RPA systems. This includes creating datasets for training computer vision algorithms and fine-tuning LLMs on specific tasks relevant to RPA use cases.
ai.buildProcess: Building a cognitive RPA system requires integrating pre-trained or custom-trained machine learning models with existing RPA frameworks. The process involves coding, testing, and deploying the AI components within the automation workflows.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the development of AI models, data labeling for training, integration with existing RPA systems, and ongoing maintenance costs related to model updates and performance optimization.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: growing adoption in enterprise back-office processes
ai.regulation: Current regulatory landscape is largely unregulated, but compliance with data protection laws (e.g., GDPR) will be crucial as cognitive RPA handles more sensitive information.
ai.risks: Risks include potential bias in AI models, security vulnerabilities related to handling sensitive data, and the need for continuous model retraining due to evolving user interfaces and business processes.
ai.profitability: Profitability is expected to grow with increasing adoption in enterprise environments where back-office automation can significantly reduce manual labor costs.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on enhancing AI capabilities, improving cross-platform compatibility, and expanding the range of tasks that cognitive RPA can handle autonomously.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. Training models for cognitive RPA requires significant computational resources, leading to higher power consumption during development.

glossary.def: Large Language Model: A type of machine learning model used for natural language processing tasks such as text generation and semantic understanding.
Robotic Process Automation: Software technology that automates routine, rule-based business processes by mimicking human interactions with software applications.

subsystems.name: Orchestrator
subsystems.role: schedules and supervises bots, manages work queues and credentials, and records what every bot did.

subsystems.name: Bot runtime
subsystems.role: executes the actual actions on a desktop, server or browser session.

subsystems.name: Screen understanding
subsystems.role: finds and identifies interface elements by meaning rather than by fixed pixel coordinates.

subsystems.name: Document understanding
subsystems.role: turns unstructured files — invoices, emails, contracts, scans — into structured fields.
parts: large language model extractor with a target schema

subsystems.name: Reasoning and action layer
subsystems.role: decides what to do next, handles exceptions and drafts outputs.
parts: retrieval over policy and procedure documents

subsystems.name: Human-in-the-loop and governance
subsystems.role: keeps a person in charge of low-confidence or high-impact decisions and monitors quality over time.

subsystems.name: Integration connectors
subsystems.role: talks to systems of record through their APIs wherever possible.

buildSteps.title: Map the process
buildSteps.detail: Record how the work is actually done, collect sample documents and screen states, and write down every exception and the success measure.

buildSteps.title: Build the deterministic spine
buildSteps.detail: Automate the stable steps first. Prefer API calls over screen clicks; use the interface only where no API exists.

buildSteps.title: Add document ingestion
buildSteps.detail: Run OCR and layout analysis on incoming files, then extract fields with a language model constrained to a fixed schema.

buildSteps.title: Replace coordinate targeting
buildSteps.detail: Identify buttons and fields from the accessibility tree where possible, falling back to vision models that recognise elements by appearance across different layouts and resolutions.

buildSteps.title: Insert the reasoning layer
buildSteps.detail: Let the model plan the next action, call permitted tools and draft text, but only within an allow-list of actions it is authorised to take.

buildSteps.title: Set confidence thresholds
buildSteps.detail: Route anything below a per-field confidence threshold, or above a risk threshold, to a human reviewer rather than letting the bot proceed.

buildSteps.title: Test against variation
buildSteps.detail: Replay historical cases and deliberately messy documents, and measure accuracy field by field, not just end to end.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Log every decision and source element, track the share of cases completed without human help, and alert on accuracy drift.

buildSteps.title: Feed corrections back
buildSteps.detail: Turn reviewer corrections into examples that improve prompts and extraction rules, then widen the scope of the process.

prerequisites.why: they provide the scheduling, credentials and execution machinery that the cognitive layer sits on top of.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with reliable tool use and structured output
prerequisites.why: they do the reading, judging and drafting that fixed rules cannot; enterprise accuracy still needs guardrails and review.

prerequisites.tech: High-accuracy OCR and document layout models
prerequisites.why: scanned and photographed paperwork must become text and tables before a model can reason about it.
identifying controls visually across many applications and resolutions works but is still brittle.

prerequisites.tech: Identity, access control and audit for AI-initiated actions
prerequisites.why: a bot acting on a real account needs permissions and traceability that satisfy auditors and regulators.

prerequisites.tech: Benchmarks and evaluation methods for agentic workflows
prerequisites.why: without agreed ways to measure multi-step task success, buyers cannot tell whether a system is safe to run unattended.

pathway.milestone: language-model features bolted onto established RPA tools for document extraction and draft generation
pathway.unlocks: handling of unstructured inputs that previously needed a person, with review queues catching errors.

pathway.milestone: semantic screen automation plus model-driven exception handling
pathway.unlocks: automations that survive interface changes and clear more cases without human help.

pathway.milestone: agentic orchestration across several systems, with policy retrieval and tool permissions as controls
pathway.unlocks: whole processes rather than single tasks, spanning email, ERP and case management.

pathway.milestone: systems that observe work, propose their own automations and are measured continuously
pathway.unlocks: rapid expansion into long-tail processes once safety and evaluation are trustworthy.
